open_points.subject: Status
open_points.text:
OQ-07 is the one earlier question still open: A5 decides the HTTPS rule, and the host and route are
carried to deployment.
open_points.question: After A9 decides that the service runs only on Linux, which part of the host decision remains for deployment: only the particular Linux machine and placement, or also the operating platform?
options: Only the particular supported Linux host and its placement remain open
The complete host choice, including operating platform, remains open
OQ-07 is partly closed and must be rewritten to separate the decided Linux platform from the remaining route and placement choices
open_points.default_guess: Treat Linux as decided by A9 and carry only the particular VPS placement, Linux environment within the clarified support baseline, and HTTPS route to deployment.

open_points.subject: A9
open_points.text: The service runs on Linux and on no other host, no version named (owner, 2026-11-21).
open_points.question: Which Linux kernel, distribution, libc, architecture, container environment and filesystem versions constitute the supported baseline?
options: Every Linux environment whose relevant calls have the required documented semantics
A named minimum kernel and a closed set of filesystems and architectures
Only the exact deployment image and host combination qualified by the deployment route
open_points.default_guess: Support only the exact deployment image and host/filesystem combination qualified by the deployment route.

witness.initial: The same deployment image is available on two Linux hosts with different kernel and filesystem implementations.
events: The deployer installs it on each host.
The service performs a placement that relies on locking, renaming and flushing.
outcomes: Both hosts are supported because both are Linux and their calls follow their own platform documentation.
Only the specifically qualified host is supported; the other deployment is outside the service contract.
witness.observer: The deployer deciding whether the installation is supported and whether a completed placement has the promised durability.

open_points.subject: A9
open_points.text:
opening without following a
   link, opening a folder as a folder, opening without blocking, creating exclusively, locking, renaming,
   flushing
open_points.question: Which exact Linux interfaces, flags, scope and guarantees do these descriptions require, including whether link refusal covers only the final component or every path component, which locking mechanism is meant, what form of rename is required, and which file and directory objects must be flushed?
options: Name the required syscalls and flags for every operation
State observable guarantees and refusal conditions that any implementation must satisfy
Leave the implementer to select any Linux mechanism matching these informal descriptions
open_points.default_guess: Specify observable guarantees and refusal conditions, then name the Linux syscall and flag combination used to realize each guarantee.

witness.initial: A requested photo is below a relative path containing a symlinked directory, while the final path component is a regular file.
events: One implementation opens the final component with O_NOFOLLOW.
Another implementation resolves the path with a mechanism that rejects every symlink component.
outcomes: The first implementation delivers the photo because the final component is not a link.
The second implementation refuses the photo because an intermediate component is a link.
witness.observer: The owner sees either a successful placement or a refusal.

open_points.subject: A9
open_points.text:
Another
   system, or a Linux or file system on which a call these rules rely on — opening without following a
   link, opening a folder as a folder, opening without blocking, creating exclusively, locking, renaming,
   flushing — does not act as Linux documents it, is unsupported
open_points.question: Which Linux documentation and version define the comparison, and how is a deployer to determine that a kernel/filesystem combination satisfies it when the service neither tests for it nor names a qualification procedure?
options: Reference a specific Linux manual/kernel version and enumerate required semantics
Require a deployment qualification test for each host and filesystem
Declare a closed supported host/filesystem matrix
open_points.default_guess: Reference a specific semantic baseline and require the deployment route to qualify the actual host and mounted filesystems against it.

witness.initial: A Linux host uses a network filesystem whose rename and flush behavior has documented filesystem-specific qualifications.
events: The deployer evaluates the host against A9.
A placement is renamed and reported complete before a host failure.
outcomes: The host is supported because its behavior follows its filesystem-specific Linux documentation.
The host is unsupported because it lacks the local-filesystem durability semantics the rule was intended to require.
witness.observer: The deployer and owner see different conclusions about whether the completed placement was covered by the service guarantees.

open_points.subject: A2
open_points.text: With one library version one source gives the same bytes.
open_points.question: Does this byte-for-byte guarantee apply across every Linux environment now admitted by A9, or only within one fully fixed deployment build including architecture and native image-codec dependencies?
options: Across all supported Linux hosts for one pinned Pillow version
Only within one immutable deployment image and architecture
Across builds only when every native and transitive codec dependency is also pinned and identical
open_points.default_guess: Limit the guarantee to one immutable deployment image and architecture, with native and transitive codec dependencies fixed.

witness.initial: Two deployment images use the same pinned direct image-library version and the same source image, but are built for supported Linux environments with different native JPEG encoder builds.
events: Each service applies the A2 operations to the same source.
Each stores the resulting JPEG and computes its sha256.
outcomes: A2 is read as requiring identical JPEG bytes and hashes across both environments.
A2 is read as guaranteeing identical bytes only within each fully fixed deployment build, so the hashes may differ.
witness.observer: The caller and Portal store observe different file hashes and potentially different placement bytes.

open_points.subject: A10
open_points.text:
- files_artifacts: APPLICABLE; references: A1, A2, A5, A6, A8; affected: M01, M02, M03, M04, connections file, source folders, Portal binary store
- concurrency: APPLICABLE; references: A3, A4, A5, A6; affected: M01, M04, M07
- dependencies: APPLICABLE; references: A9; affected: image library, web framework, validation library, web server
open_points.question: Which security-review category explicitly covers A9's new Linux kernel and filesystem assumptions for link-safe opening, exclusive creation, locking, rename and flush behavior, and which affected surfaces must it name?
options: Add A9 and the Linux/filesystem boundary to files_artifacts
Extend dependencies to name the operating platform, kernel and filesystem
Add a separate platform/filesystem category with an explicit outcome
State with a rationale that the new support assumption is outside every security category
open_points.default_guess: Add A9 to files_artifacts and name the Linux host, mounted source folders, persistence location and Portal binary store as affected; also name the platform dependency under dependencies.

witness.initial: A10 is used to decide whether State 3 may start after the new A9 rule is accepted.
events: A reviewer runs the stated design lint.
The existing category lines remain unchanged and the lint reports no finding.
outcomes: The security review is complete because dependencies already references A9 as a whole.
The security review is incomplete because no explicit category outcome evaluates the new kernel and filesystem trust assumptions.
witness.observer: The reviewer or State 3 gate sees either permission to proceed or an unresolved security category.
